# Why we read the scientific record {.page-title}

[Research is one of the best tools we have to improve health. But it is hard to see the whole picture: what has been done, by whom, and what is still missing. We help make that picture clear.]{.lead}
:::

[Who is behind it]{.eyebrow}

## Maxime Descartes Mbogning Fonkou
:::

::: {.reveal}
I started my career in clinical microbiology labs in Yaoundé, Marseille and Paris. I studied the bacteria that live in the human respiratory tract and gut, and helped describe new bacterial species. The lab taught me how evidence is built: one careful step at a time.

Over the years, a bigger question grew in my mind. What does all this research add up to? Who does it, who pays for it, and who is left out? I followed that question into the science of science, at York University and Simon Fraser University, working on research mapping, patent analysis and research evaluation.

CognosX is how I continue that work. The idea is simple: help people read the scientific record clearly, so that money and effort go where they matter most. I care especially about health problems that affect Africa and other places that research too often overlooks.

I work in English and French, from Burnaby, Canada.

[What guides the work]{.eyebrow}

## Three principles
:::

::: {.grid .grid-3}
::: {.card-cx .reveal}
### Careful, then fast

AI helps us work at scale, but people check the results. We say how accurate the method is, not only what it found.
:::

::: {.card-cx .reveal}
### Context over counts

Numbers alone can mislead. We use indicators responsibly and explain what they can and cannot show.
:::

::: {.card-cx .reveal}
### Fair and global

We look at who is missing from the picture, not only who leads it, and we listen to people where the research happens.
:::
